pathInstructions.instructions: The rule text here and src/publish/sanitize.ts move together (AGENTS.md): a change to what the model may write must keep src/engine/rule-file.test.ts's example findings representative, because those examples round-trip through the real sanitizer and are the only mechanism keeping the two aligned.

A check tightened here can silently discard a correct finding before publication — the failure is a finding nobody ever sees, not a visible error. Verify src/engine/rule-file.test.ts still round-trips its example findings.

classify() and buildRuleFile() resolve include/exclude overlap in OPPOSITE directions, and getting it wrong has broken production once. classify() checks generated first, then review-relevance, and falls back to excluded last; the engine's own layering lets exclude beat include. Re-read the other before changing either.

Every digest here must come from the upstream release's own sha256sum.txt for the named version tag. A digest that does not match what the tag actually publishes turns the integrity check into a rubber stamp.

This file is the frozen qualification corpus. A changed case invalidates comparability with every recorded qualification, so a change here needs its own full corpus wave and an evidence file saying so.

A committed build artifact. It must be regenerated from the source in the same change (npm run verify), never hand-edited: consumers execute this file, and a bundle that differs from its reviewed source is the near-miss check:bundle exists to catch.
